subject: Critical Thinking
title: Voltaire and the Power of Satire
description: A micro-lesson that makes Voltaire and the Power of Satire usable.

hook.text: A French writer was beaten by aristocrats' thugs. He responded by becoming the most dangerous pen in Europe.

buildup.text: Voltaire used satire, irony, and wit to attack the Church, monarchy, and dogma. Candide mocked blind optimism.

discovery.text: His method: reduce an opponent's position to its absurd conclusions. If logic leads to nonsense, the premise fails.

twist.text: Voltaire never built a system. He destroyed bad ones — critical thinking can be demolition, not construction.

climax.text: His phrase 'Écrasez l'infâme' (crush the infamous) became the Enlightenment's battle cry against superstition.

punchline.text: Sometimes the sharpest argument is a joke.

quiz.question: What was Voltaire's primary critical thinking method?
options: Using satire to reduce positions to absurd conclusions

details.summary: Voltaire used wit, satire, and ridicule to expose the absurdities of religious dogma, political tyranny, and philosophical pretension. His weapon was laughter, and he showed that humor can be a devastatingly effective form of critical thinking.
details.whyItMatters: Voltaire demonstrated that critical thinking need not be dry or academic. Satire reaches audiences that formal arguments cannot and holds power accountable through exposure.
takeaways: Satire is a form of argument that uses humor to expose absurdity
Voltaire targeted religious intolerance and political abuse
His work showed that ridicule can be more powerful than logic alone

faq.question: How did Voltaire use satire as a critical thinking tool?
faq.answer: In works like Candide, Voltaire created absurd scenarios that followed the logic of his opponents to ridiculous conclusions. By showing where ideas led when taken seriously, he exposed their flaws more memorably than formal refutation could.

faq.question: Why is satire considered a powerful but dangerous form of criticism?
faq.answer: Satire is powerful because it makes foolishness visible to everyone. It is dangerous because it humiliates its targets, who may retaliate. Voltaire himself was imprisoned and exiled multiple times for his satirical writings.
